parameters.formDescription: Enter a post topic and scheduled publish time. The workflow will generate copy, composite a brand image, and send it for human approval before publishing.

values.placeholder: e.g. How AI is transforming social media marketing

nodes.name: Form Trigger
nodes.notes: ENTRY POINT — Serves a web form at the workflow's production URL. The submitter enters a post topic and a scheduled publish time. These arrive in the next node as $json.topic and $json.scheduled_at.

nodes.name: Generate Post Content
nodes.notes: LLM GENERATION + RETRY — Calls Groq Llama 3.3 70B (free tier) with a system instruction enforcing 90-150 words. On each failed attempt, appends a corrective user turn telling the model its word count and asking for a full rewrite. STRICT: if still out of range after 5 attempts, the node throws and the workflow stops, so a non-compliant post can never reach approval or publishing. Returns: { topic, scheduled_at, copy, wordCount, attempts, withinRange }

nodes.name: Compose Brand Image
nodes.notes: IMAGE COMPOSITING — POSTs the post topic to FastAPI /compose-image. FastAPI runs Pillow to overlay the topic text onto the brand card template at fixed pixel coordinates. Returns JSON: { image_url: '/output/abc123.png', image_path: '...' }. Replace REPLACE_WITH_NGROK_URL with your current ngrok URL.

nodes.name: Request Human Approval
nodes.notes: HITL REQUEST — Creates a pending review in FastAPI. The key field is resume_webhook_url = $execution.resumeUrl, which is n8n's auto-generated webhook URL for this exact execution. When the human clicks Approve/Edit/Reject in the dashboard, FastAPI POSTs to that URL, which resumes this paused execution. Returns: { review_id, review_url }.

nodes.name: Wait for Human Decision
nodes.notes: WORKFLOW PAUSE — n8n literally suspends this execution here. No polling, no CPU usage. The execution is stored on disk and resumed only when FastAPI POSTs the decision payload to $execution.resumeUrl. When resumed, the POST body ({ decision, final_copy, review_id }) becomes $json for the next node.

nodes.name: Was Approved?
nodes.notes: DECISION BRANCH — True output (top): publish to Facebook then Instagram. False output (bottom): log rejection and stop. The $json.decision value is 'approved' or 'rejected', sent by FastAPI when the human clicked a button on the review dashboard.

nodes.name: Publish to Facebook
nodes.notes: MOCK FACEBOOK PUBLISH — Calls the FastAPI mock endpoint. Uses final_copy from the approval callback (which may be the human-edited version if the reviewer used Edit & Approve). The FastAPI server logs the full payload to the terminal — check your console to confirm it fired. Replace REPLACE_WITH_NGROK_URL in both the URL and the image_url value.

nodes.name: Publish to Instagram
nodes.notes: MOCK INSTAGRAM PUBLISH — Same as Facebook but targets the Instagram mock endpoint. Runs after Facebook. Both log to the FastAPI terminal — this is what to show in the demo video to prove the publish step worked.

nodes.name: Rejected — Log and Stop
nodes.notes: REJECTION PATH — Sets a clear status and stops. No publish happens. You can see in the n8n execution history that this node ran, which proves the reject path worked correctly.
